anchoredObservation: Native HTML/PDF page 2 and bound DE/EN input say only that the learner can explain aromatic reactivity. The German word fachlich supplies no chemical relationship, and both versions largely restate the title.
hypothesizedMechanism: A coach can treat a reaction-name statement as explaining reactivity because no explanatory relationship is named in the learner-facing competence, while the actual native image already relies on aromatic restoration.
violatedCriterion: General D v2: make the claimed competence sufficiently informative for teaching toward understanding; a bounded revision may name an essential reason or model relationship already within the goal. Chemistry criteria: independent explanation must expose the chemical relationship.
minimalCounterexample: A learner answers: Aromaten reagieren durch elektrophile Substitution. This names a reaction route but supplies no reason from the aromatic electronic structure; a literal title-restatement reading can count it as the requested explanation.
counterarguments: The bound Q1.1 LK chapter, prerequisite MO goal and V2 understanding evidence can supply the missing relationship during teaching.
The current sentence is not a false chemical statement; the problem is local explanatory specificity, not a new source or scientific fault.
proposedLocalChange: Die lernende Person kann die Reaktivität aromatischer Systeme anhand ihrer Elektronendelokalisierung begründen. / The learner can explain the reactivity of aromatic systems in terms of their electron delocalization.
possibleSideEffects: The new text and affected page, D records and other semantic-fingerprint evidence need fresh bindings after an accepted wording change.
Do not require a new MO construction competency or make electrophilic substitution compulsory in every national/GK scope.
broaderEvidenceNeeded: Resolve this exact description candidate separately. HE KCGO 21.04.2026 S.38 Q1.1 LK supports the mesomerie-based structure/reactivity relationship; it does not establish full national source mapping or actual learner understanding.
